newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wages only one factor in Australian jobless-Reith.
newsitem.headline: Wages only one factor in Australian jobless-Reith.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Thursday wages was only one factor of many that were affecting unemployment.
"If we are to get unemployment down, people need to understand the whole range of factors that affect it," Reith told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"That (wages) is a factor that affects the level of unemployment -- there are, of course, others."
Reith had been asked why Prime Minister John Howard in recent days had repeatedly raised the link between high unemployment levels and high minimum wages.
Howard said on Tuesday there was no need to change minimum wages, but the community needed to understand the impact that wages had on jobs.
After travelling to the United States and the United Kingdom earlier this month, Howard attributed a much lower unemployment rate in the U.S. to lower minimum wages there.
"He (Howard) made the point when he was overseas that one of the factors that affect unemployment in both countries and in Australia is the minimum wage level that they have in place," Reith said.
"That is simply a statement of fact. He did not raise it as a precursor to a change in the federal government's policy."
Australia's unemployment rate has been stuck above 8.5 percent since Howard's conservative Liberal-National coalition was elected in March 1996.
Unemployment rose to 8.8 percent in May and economists are expecting the jobless rate to be 8.7 percent in June when data is released later on Thursday.
